subject.title: [Bug] v2026.5.22 启动后 Gateway CPU 持续 100%+，导致请求延迟飙升 50-100 倍

question: Should normal gateway startup stop scheduling provider-auth prewarm by default while keeping explicit opt-in startup warm and auth-profile failure rewarm hooks?
rationale: Current main and the latest release still run the startup warm by default, and disabling it improves startup responsiveness but changes when provider-auth availability is eagerly prepared.

options.title: Make startup prewarm default-off
options.body: Land the hook-only/default-off behavior from the canonical startup PR and rely on explicit opt-in or failure-triggered rewarm for eager auth-state preparation.

options.title: Keep eager startup warm
options.body: Keep the current default-on startup warm and close the linked PRs only if maintainers accept the reported startup CPU/latency tradeoff.

options.title: Require a narrower live repro first
options.body: Hold the issue open until a current-main macOS reproduction confirms whether the worker-thread mitigation still leaves user-visible CPU or RPC latency.

recommendation.title: Make startup prewarm default-off
recommendation.body: Land the hook-only/default-off behavior from the canonical startup PR and rely on explicit opt-in or failure-triggered rewarm for eager auth-state preparation.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the open maintainer PR carrying the default-off startup contract and platform proof for the same provider-auth prewarm path.
